propositions.statement: Let p be any prime, K any field of characteristic p, λ an integer with 0≤λ<p, V=V(λ) the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂-module of dimension λ+1, and x,y,h its Chevalley operators satisfying hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h. Let v∈V be nonzero with xv=0 and hv=λv. Let U_ℤ be the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r!, r≥0. Let M⊆V be any U_ℤ-stable free abelian subgroup with an integer basis also a complex basis of V. The target space is M⊗_ℤ K with the induced x,y,h actions and the Chevalley Lie algebra (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, including characteristic two.

For every natural t, h(y^t v)=(ell−2t)y^t v, and for t≥1, x(y^t v)=t(ell−t+1)y^(t−1)v. For 0≤t≤ell, x^t y^t v=t!·(∏_{a=0}^{t−1}(ell−a))v≠0, where the product at t=0 is one and all coefficients are taken in ℂ. For every i∈J, e_i≠0 and h(e_i)=(ell−2i)e_i. The function J→ℂ taking i to ell−2i is injective.
propositions.origin: basis-proof.md:3, commutator inductions and nonvanishing before eigenvector independence.

propositions.statement: The family (e_i)_(i∈J) is a complex basis of V. One has y^(ell+1)v=0, and y^t v=0 for every natural t≥ell+1. Its generator actions are x e_0=0, x e_i=(ell−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤ell, y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<ell, y e_ell=0, and h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i for all i∈J.
propositions.origin: basis-proof.md:3, basis by B001/B002, termination, and generator formulas.

propositions.statement: The family (e_i)_(i∈J) is a complex basis of V. For every natural r and i∈J, X_r e_i=binom(ell−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and equals zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤ell and equals zero if i+r>ell. All binomial coefficients in these formulas are natural binomial coefficients mapped to ℂ. The subscript of an e vector is used only in the branch in which it lies in J.
propositions.origin: basis-proof.md:3, final divided-power calculation; N001 label retained.

propositions.statement: Every s_ij is an integer-linear endomorphism of the original lattice M. For all i,j,k,l∈J, s_ij s_kl=δ_jk ell! s_il, and ∑_(i∈J) s_ii=ell! Id_M, where δ_jk is 1 when j=k and 0 otherwise. For every natural r, r! A_r=(A_1)^r and r! B_r=(B_1)^r in End_ℤ(M). More precisely, in the complex basis e, the complex operator j!(ell−j)! X_(ell−i)Y_ell X_ell Y_(ell−j) sends e_k to ell! e_i if k=j and to zero otherwise, and its restriction to M is s_ij.
propositions.origin: basis-proof.md:5, integral scaled matrix units; use only restrictions of integral operators.

propositions.statement: For every integer basis (b_i)_(i∈J) of M, the vectors 1⊗b_i form a K-basis of Q. In particular Q is finite dimensional, dim_K Q=ell+1>0, and Q is nonzero. The map τ:V_K→Q is a K-linear isomorphism, with inverse a⊗u↦u⊗a. For every f∈End_ℤ(M), τ∘(f⊗Id_K)=Fext(f)∘τ. Consequently V_K is also nonzero of K-dimension ell+1. In particular this intertwining applies to f=A_1=x|M, f=B_1=y|M, and f=h|M=A_1 B_1−B_1 A_1.

binders.type: integer basis of M indexed by J

propositions.origin: basis-proof.md:7 and 13, actual base-changed lattice basis, dimension, scalar-compatible flip and all operator identifications.

propositions.statement: The canonical map Fext is a unital ℤ-algebra homomorphism End_ℤ(M)→End_K(Q). For each natural r≤ell, (r!:K) is a unit and is nonzero; in particular d≠0. For these r, (r!:K) Fext(A_r)=Fext(A_1)^r and (r!:K) Fext(B_r)=Fext(B_1)^r. For all i,j,k,l∈J the normalized endomorphisms satisfy U_ij U_kl=δ_jk U_il, and ∑_(i∈J) U_ii=Id_Q, with δ_jk=1 if j=k and zero otherwise. These assertions include ell=0.
propositions.origin: basis-proof.md:7–9, B004/B005 base change and factorial normalization.

propositions.statement: One has d≠0, U_ij U_kl=δ_jk U_il for all i,j,k,l∈J, and ∑_(i∈J)U_ii=Id_Q, with δ_jk=1 if j=k and 0 otherwise. Every K-linear subspace W⊆Q satisfying Fext(A_1)(W)⊆W and Fext(B_1)(W)⊆W satisfies U_ij(W)⊆W for all i,j∈J. This holds for ell=0 and uses no distinctness of reduced h-eigenvalues or algebraic closure of K.
propositions.origin: basis-proof.md:9; N004 label retained for normalized units and invariant-subspace preservation.

propositions.statement: For every field F, positive natural n, finite-dimensional F-vector space T with dim_F T=n, and endomorphisms C_ij∈End_F(T) indexed by i,j∈Fin n satisfying C_ij C_kl=δ_jk C_il for all indices and ∑_i C_ii=Id_T, every F-linear subspace Z⊆T preserved by all C_ij is zero or all T. Here δ_jk is 1 if j=k and 0 otherwise, and products mean composition with the right factor acting first.
propositions.origin: basis-proof.md:11, standalone matrix-unit simplicity; the choices of nonzero vector, diagonal index and independent family remain in one proof unit.

propositions.statement:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

For every complex vector space V, every index type I, endomorphism f, injective eigenvalue family μ:I→ℂ, and family a:I→V of nonzero f-eigenvectors with f(a_i)=μ_i a_i, the family a is complex-linearly independent.

hypotheses: V is a complex vector space and f is a complex-linear endomorphism.
For every i∈I, a_i≠0 and f(a_i)=μ_i a_i.
